moves.comment: Take the centre. This starts the London: one safe set-up you can use against most Black replies.

children.comment: Bring the bishop out before e3 closes it in. This is the key London idea.
Guard d4 and f4 and free your f1 bishop. Your bishop on f4 is now safe.
Develop a knight. It guards d4 and e5.
Their bishop attacks yours. Step back to g3. If they take, retake with the h-pawn. Then the h-file is half open for your rook.
Develop your last knight. From d2 it supports e4, which you can push later.
Guard d4 again. The pawns on c3, d4 and e3 are your London base.
Aim the bishop at h7 and get ready to castle.
Castle. Your king is safe and your rook joins the game.
Knight to e5. The d4 pawn and the bishop on g3 guard it. If ...Nxe5, dxe5 attacks the bishop and the knight.
Retake with the pawn. It attacks the bishop on d6 and the knight on f6, and Black cannot save both.
Black saves the bishop. But the pawn on e5 still attacks the knight on f6.
Take the knight with the pawn. If Black takes back, you are still a knight ahead for a pawn.
Black takes the pawn, but you are still a knight up for a pawn.
Bring the queen into play and keep it simple. You are a knight up for a pawn, so the position is winning.
Black trades bishops.
Retake with the h-pawn. The h-file is half open for your rook, and g4 can start a kingside attack later.
Aim the bishop at h7, next to Black's king. Get ready to castle.
Develop your last knight. From d2 it supports e4.
Guard d4 and keep the centre solid. Then you can play Ne5 or g4.
Black attacks your d4 pawn. It is safe: the c3 pawn, the e3 pawn and the f3 knight all guard it.
Jump to e5, the favourite London square. From there the knight eyes d7 and f7.
Black controls g5. The king cannot use h7 yet, because your d3 bishop covers it.
Start your kingside attack. If g5 hxg5, no pawn is left on the h-file and your rooks can use it.
Aim the bishop at h7 and get ready to castle.
Develop your last knight. It supports e4.
Guard d4 again. Your pawns on c3, d4 and e3 are the London base.
Castle. Now your pieces are ready for Ne5 or a quiet plan with Qe2 and e4.
Knight to e5, guarded by the d4 pawn. It attacks the c6 knight, which has no guard, and if ...Nxe5, dxe5 hits the f6 knight.
Black brings out the last minor piece. All four black minor pieces are now developed.
The queen eyes the d5 pawn and guards your bishop on f4.
Black takes the knight on e5 to remove your active piece.
Take back with the d-pawn. The pawn on e5 attacks the knight on f6.
The knight jumps away from the pawn. It now attacks your knight on d2.
Guard the knight on d2. The black knight attacks it and nothing guards it yet.
Guard d4 first. Do not take on c5 yet.
Develop your last knight. It supports e4 and guards b3.
Their bishop attacks yours. Step back to g3. If they take, retake with hxg3.
Aim the bishop at h7 and get ready to castle.
Black attacks b2.
Guard b2 with the queen and offer a trade. c3 has opened c2, so the queen can reach b3.
Black hits your queen and gains space.
Trade queens. The attack on b2 is gone.
Develop calmly. The c4 pawn controls d3, so the bishop goes to e2, and you can castle next.
An easy slip: Black puts the bishop where your bishop on f4 attacks it. Nothing guards it.
Take the free bishop. No black piece can take back on d6.
Black trades queens. Take back on b3.
Retake with the knight. Your pawns stay healthy: you get no doubled b-pawns.
The black pawn attacks your knight on b3 and gains space on the queenside.
Bring the knight back. From d2 it eyes the c4 pawn and the e4 square.
Black guards the c4 pawn with the b-pawn.
A quiet move with a purpose: h3 takes the g4 square away from the black knight.
Black hits d4 early.
Guard d4 again. If Black takes on d4, you can take back with the c-pawn or the e-pawn.
Develop a knight. It guards d4 and e5.
Develop your last knight. It supports e4. Now you reach the main London set-up.
Black copies your bishop move.
Develop a knight. It guards d4 and e5.
Offer a trade. Their bishop on f5 sits on the same diagonal. If they take, retake and keep developing.
Retake with the queen. It stays central and eyes b5. Castle next.
Trade your bishop for theirs. This removes their active bishop, and you keep developing.
Develop your last knight. It supports e4.
Guard d4. Castle next.
Black tries a pawn break too early.
Take the free pawn. Nothing guards e5, and your bishop is safe for now.
Their knight attacks your bishop. Retreat to g3. You stay a pawn up.
Kick the knight away. This also guards d4.
Black hits d4 at once. This is the most testing reply to the London.
Guard d4 and f4. If ...cxd4, retake with the e-pawn.
Guard d4 again. It also opens c2, so your queen can reach b3 if Black plays ...Qb6.
Black hits b2. Stay calm.
Guard b2 and offer a queen trade. You do not lose a pawn.
Black attacks your queen and gains space.
Trade queens. The attack on b2 is gone.
Develop the knight. It attacks the c4 pawn and supports a later e4 push.
Push e4. It attacks the bishop on f5 and the pawn on d5.
Black takes the e4 pawn with the bishop. Your knight on d2 guards e4, so you can take back.
Take the bishop with the knight. If Black takes it with the d-pawn, the c4 pawn loses its guard.
Black takes the knight. The d-pawn leaves d5, so it no longer guards c4.
Take the loose pawn. Material is level: you gave a knight and a pawn, Black gave a bishop and a pawn.
Black takes.
Trade queens before you take back on d4. After ...axb6, Black has doubled b-pawns.
Retake with the pawn. Your centre is solid.
Develop the knight. It guards d4 and e5.
Black takes your queen. Take back, and the queens are traded.
Retake with the a-pawn. The a-file opens for your rook, and your pawns are still fine.
Black hits b2 right away.
Guard b2 with the queen. You cannot play Qb3 yet, because the pawn on c2 is in the way.
Develop a knight. It guards d4, which the c5 pawn and the c6 knight attack.
Retake with the pawn. Now d4 has two attackers and one guard, so play c3 soon.
Guard d4 once more. Then develop the f1 bishop and castle.
Black brings the bishop out before ...e6 closes its diagonal.
Not Bd3: the bishop on f5 would take it and nothing of yours guards d3. The bishop is safe on e2.
Black guards d5 and f5 and unblocks the f8 bishop.
Develop your last minor piece. The knight eyes the c4 and e4 squares.
Black copies you. Both sides have the same ideas.
Guard d4 and f4. Now the bishop on f4 is safe.
Develop a knight. It guards d4 and e5.
Offer a trade. If they take on d3, retake and your pieces stay safe.
Retake with the queen. It stays central and eyes b5. Castle next.
Trade your bishop for theirs. This removes their active bishop, and you keep developing.
Develop your last knight. It supports e4.
Guard d4. Castle next.
Develop a knight. It guards d4 and e5.
Offer a trade. If they take on d3, retake with the queen. This move order reaches the main line.
Guard d4 and f4. Now the bishop on f4 is safe.
Black wants to trade your bishop.
Step back. If Black takes on g3, retake with hxg3.
Develop a knight. It guards d4 and e5.
Develop your last knight. It supports e4.
Guard d4 again. Your pawns on c3, d4 and e3 are your base.
Black eyes d4 and the b4 square.
Guard d4 and f4 and free the f1 bishop.
Black's bishop attacks your queen.
Take it for free. Nothing guards the bishop on g4.
Black's knight eyes c2 and a2.
Kick the knight. It must leave b4, and c3 also guards d4.
Develop a knight. It guards d4 and e5.
Develop a knight. It guards d4 and e5.
Their bishop pins your knight to the queen. Be2 develops and breaks the pin: the queen no longer stands behind the knight.
Ask the bishop a question. It must trade on f3 or retreat.
Guard d4. It also stops ...Nb4.
Their bishop attacks yours. Trade it and keep a simple game.
Develop your last knight. It supports e4.
Castle. Your king is safe and your pieces are ready.
Black strikes in the centre. The pawn attacks your d4 pawn.
Take the pawn. Now your e5 pawn attacks the queen on d6 and the knight on f6.
Black retakes with the knight. The queen on d6 guards it.
Trade the knights. Now the black bishop on h5 attacks your bishop on e2.
Black retakes with the queen, which now stands in the centre.
Take the bishop on h5. It attacked your bishop on e2, so you trade it off.
Black trades the h5 bishop for your knight on f3.
Retake with the d2 knight. On f3 it guards d4 and watches e5.
Black hits your d4 pawn with the e-pawn.
The queen attacks the b7 pawn, which no black piece guards. It also eyes d5.
Offer a bishop trade. Their bishop on f5 is on the same diagonal. If they take, retake and develop.
Retake with the queen. It stays central and eyes b5. Castle next.
Guard d4 and stop ...Nb4. Castle next.
Bring the bishop out first. The London works against almost every set-up.
Guard d4 and f4 and free your f1 bishop. Your bishop on f4 is now safe.
Develop a knight. It guards d4 and e5.
Bishop to d3 hits the g6 pawn. Castle soon to keep your king safe.
h3 stops ...Bg4 and ...Ng4. If ...Nh5, retreat the bishop to h2.
Develop your last knight. It supports e4.
Guard d4. The pawns on c3, d4 and e3 are your base.
Castle. Your king is safe and you can plan e4 next.
The black bishop now looks at your knight on f3. The knight is well guarded.
Keep the bishop safe from ...e5 and ...Nh5. On h2 it stays on the same diagonal.
Black backs up the ...e5 push with a rook on the e-file.
Rook to e1. It backs the e3 pawn and prepares your e4 break.
Black attacks your bishop.
Keep your bishop. It stays on the b8-h2 diagonal.
Develop your last knight. It supports e4.
Black attacks your d4 pawn with the e-pawn.
Guard d4 once more: the c3 pawn, the e3 pawn and the f3 knight now guard it.
Black adds the queen behind the e5 pawn.
Castle. Your king is safe and your rook joins the game.
Black attacks your d4 pawn with the c-pawn. The g7 bishop also hits d4, so it is attacked twice.
Add a guard to d4: the c3 pawn, the e3 pawn and the f3 knight guard it.
Black takes on d4. Now you choose how to retake.
Retake with the c-pawn. Your e3 pawn stays and guards d4, and the c-file opens for your rooks.
Black plays ...d5 and transposes into the main lines.
Guard d4 and f4. You are back in the main London.
Develop a knight. It guards d4 and e5.
Guard d4 and f4 and free your f1 bishop.
Guard d4 again. The pawns on c3, d4 and e3 are your base.
Develop a knight. It guards d4 and e5.
Develop your last knight. It supports e4.
Their bishop attacks yours. Step back to g3. If they take, retake with hxg3.
Aim the bishop at h7 and get ready to castle.
Black hits d4 and may attack b2 next.
Guard d4 and f4.
Black hits b2.
Guard b2 with the queen. You cannot play Qb3, because c2 is in the way.
Retake with the pawn: it is the only capture. Your queen guards b2, but nothing guards d4 now, so if ...Qxd4, play Nf3 and hit the queen.
Develop first. If ...cxd4, take the pawn back with the knight.
Retake with the knight. It sits in the centre.
Develop a knight and hit the centre.
Trade a pair of knights to simplify.
Take the centre. Your knight on c3 supports the e4 pawn.
Support d4 first. If ...cxd4, retake with the pawn and the bishop gets free.
Retake with the pawn. Now the bishop can come out.
Develop the bishop outside your pawns. It is free now, and it eyes the b8-h2 diagonal.
Support d4. Your pawns on c3 and d4 give a solid centre, and the c3 pawn takes b4 from the c6 knight.
Offer a bishop trade. Their bishop on f5 is on the same diagonal.
Black takes the bishop on d3. Your queen guards d3, so you can retake.
Retake with the queen. It is the only piece that can take on d3.
Black guards d5 and unblocks the f8 bishop.
Develop your last knight. It eyes the e4 and c4 squares.
Black takes space in the centre.
Guard d4 and keep things solid. Your c1 bishop is now behind the e3 pawn; it can go to f4 only after the e-pawn leaves e3, for example after ...cxd4 exd4.
Guard d4 again. Your pawns on c3, d4 and e3 are your base.
Black prepares ...d5: the e6 pawn would guard it.
Guard d4 and open the f1 bishop.
Develop the bishop toward the kingside. Castle next.
Black attacks d4 a second time.
Guard d4 again. If ...cxd4, retake with the pawn.
Black offers a pawn. This is the Englund Gambit.
Take the pawn. Black will try to win time, so develop quickly.
Develop and guard the e5 pawn.
Black attacks the e5 pawn again.
Add another guard to e5 and develop the bishop.
Black checks and attacks both b2 and your f4 bishop.
Block the check and attack the queen.
Develop a knight. Black's queen is far from home, and Rb1 or Nd5 can chase it.
The knight attacks the queen on b6, and most queen moves allow Nxc7+, a fork of the king and the a8 rook. Your pieces are far ahead in development.
Black wants the pawn back.
Take another pawn. Black will retake and you stay a pawn up.
Develop a knight and keep your extra pawn.
The Dutch Defense. Black grabs space on the kingside.
Bring the bishop out before e3 closes it in.
Guard d4 and f4 and free your f1 bishop.
Develop a knight. It guards d4 and e5.
h3 stops ...Ng4, which would hit e3. Your bishop also gets h2 as a retreat.
Bishop to d3 hits the f5 pawn. Castle soon.
Develop your last knight. It supports e4, which can hit the f5 pawn.
